Market balance & price outlook 14 © 2012 CRU International Limited confidential # Growing resource nationalism and local opposition to mining due to environmental issues #### **Ore grade problems** - Likelihood of major copper mine disruptions • Seasonal decline in ore grades Q1 2012 but 2% improvement y-o-y. - Ore grades increased by 17% q-o-q at Escondida, helping push up the regional average in S&C America. #### **Labour** - 10-day strike at Doe Runs’s Cobriza operation in Peru - 2-day strike by contract workers at Escondida. - Additional strike threats at Grasberg #### **Governance issues** #### **Mergers & acquisitions** - Indonesia implements 20% tax on mineral exports. - Chile drafts a land-rights law for indigenous populations. - Local opposition to mining operations in Peru and Chile due to environmental issues. - Xstrata shareholder, Qatar, is asking for better terms in merger deal Glencore and Xstrata. - Cumbres Andinas acquire a 70% stake in Mina Justa - Anglo American and Codelco in out-of-court talks. #### **Natural hazards** #### **Infrastructure** - The Los Bronces mine in Chile affected by snowfall - The Chile-Peru border area was hit by two earthquakes. but no damages or disruptions have been reported. - Operations in the DRC struggling with power outages. - Securing power supply is a key challenge for the future. ##### **High likelihood** ##### **Medium likelihood** ##### **Low likelihood** ###### Data: CRU 15 © 2012 CRU International Limited confidential # Ore grades decline again in Q1 2012 ### Q1 2006 – Q1 2012 Sample Total Cu Production (000t) Sample average

Data: Oxford Economics, CRU 41 © 2012 CRU International Limited confidential # Key risks to the price outlook : Most supply risks to the price are to the upside. Tight availability of equipment, qualified personnel, water, power, etc. mean that **sequencing of projects** (by companies and the industry) will be a serious challenge. In addition, the increasing level of challenges to projects (mine and smelter/refinery) from government and community relations could lead to lower output than forecast. There is some downside production risk. If our **macroeconomic forecast turns out to be too optimistic** , then demand could be less and the wave of mine projects could come on to swamp the market and drive down prices sooner than in our base case. : The key risk to the copper price is the uncertainty of how the global economy will perform. The apparent **improvement in the US could prove short-lived and China could possibly not see a return to higher growth in H2 2012** . The Eurozone crisis could also still prompt more financial market turmoil, including a stronger US$ and lower dollar denominated prices for copper. On the other hand, tightness in the forward curve shows that another squeeze could be engineered to boost prices in the next 6 months. Economic growth in the **US and China could also prove stronger** than in the base

case.  This would be positive for growth, providing upside potential for prices. 



: We now expect that **aluminium will make more inroads into the insulated power cable market** as a result of an increase in aluminium wirerod capacity available to target this segment by 2015. CRU forecasts that the ratio of the **copper price to that of aluminium will average close to 4:1** , which will weigh on consumers’ strategic decision-making. 



: Any scrap shortage for direct use would lead to higher refined consumption.  A double-dip recession in the developed world would accelerate the de-coupling of emerging markets and favour copper-intensive domestic demand.  Any substantial fall in the price could also lead to buying by the SRB or some Chinese consumers or speculators that rate copper as a bargain.
